title: Spike: verify Sportmonks/API-Football coverage + latency before contract specs
description: Blocking spike for the Contract specs epic (wp-y08). wp-gpo.3's interview set Sportmonks as spec.md's working-assumption provider (API-Football as documented fallback, Highlightly de-prioritized), based on ~/Downloads/whoplayd-provider-research.md — a doc-only evaluation with 5 items that can't be settled without a live trial key. Those items must be verified before proxy-contract.md / sighting-schema.md are written against a specific response shape.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Sportmonks: confirm Scottish League One and League Two are actually selectable in the leagues list, and which plan tier is required alongside the English tiers + both domestic cups + 3 UEFA competitions.
2. API-Football: pull lineups/player-statistics for a handful of real League Two and Scottish League Two fixtures and confirm minutes-played is populated (not just present as a schema field).
3. All three candidates: time how long after full-time a finished match's lineup/minutes actually appears, for at least one lower-league fixture.
4. Sportmonks: clarify what '2,000/2,500/3,000 calls per entity per hour' gates in practice (feeds retry-worker backoff design).
5. Highlightly (only if still in consideration): get written confirmation that a normal app backend/proxy doesn't trip the ToS 6.1 'proxy or pass-through' restriction.

title: Interview: spec.md (Plan Mode vs constitution)
description: First step of spec.md. Plan Mode interview against the constitution to gather product requirements and resolve/assign the Open Questions (provider choice, Scottish cutoff, discovery navigation shape, recent-vs-historical boundary) before drafting.
acceptance_criteria: Interview findings captured, sufficient to draft spec.md.
notes:
Interview findings (2026-09-11), sourced partly from user-supplied ~/Downloads/whoplayd-provider-research.md:

1. PROVIDER: Sportmonks = working assumption (best documented League Two coverage, 99.99% uptime claim, least-concerning ToS on proxy/backend use; likely needs the EUR99/mo Growth tier for ~11-13 competitions since Starter caps at 5 leagues). API-Football = documented fallback (cheaper, explicit League Two + all 4 Scottish tiers, but hedges on lineup/stat depth 'may vary by season/fixture'). Highlightly de-prioritized (unconfirmed lower-league coverage; ToS 6.1 bars proxy/pass-through use without permission, conflicting with WhoPlayd's core proxy architecture). 5 unverified items tracked in new spike wp-y08.5, blocking wp-y08.1/.2/.3 (not blocking spec.md drafting).

2. RECENT VS HISTORICAL BOUNDARY: rolling 7-day window. Date-anchored discovery = last ~7 days; older routes to historical browse.

3. HISTORICAL NAV SHAPE: two parallel entry axes — Team -> Year -> all fixtures for that team (season-ticket-holder recall pattern), OR Year -> Competition (day-tripper / one-off recall pattern). Not a single forced axis.

4. SCOTTISH CUTOFF: aspirational target = as deep as England (Premiership/Championship/League One/League Two), contingent on wp-y08.5 spike. API-Football already confirms all 4 tiers; Sportmonks only confirms Premiership publicly today — if spike shows Sportmonks can't reach League One/Two, the API-Football fallback path is what preserves this depth target.
close_reason: Interview complete — provider, recent/historical boundary, historical nav shape, and Scottish cutoff all resolved. Findings captured in issue notes + bd remember. Spike wp-y08.5 created for the 5 unverified provider items, blocking wp-y08.1/.2/.3.

title: Interview: bootstrapping approach & sequencing
description: First step of Repo bootstrapping. Decide sequencing/process before any mechanical work: commit timing (e.g. finalize .gitignore before the first commit), confirm locked tooling (npm workspaces, ESLint+Prettier), WSL/Metro caveats, workspace layout specifics.
acceptance_criteria: Bootstrapping sequencing/process decisions captured; mechanical items cleared to execute.
notes:
Bootstrapping sequencing/process decisions (interview output):

APP / FILESYSTEM (web-first):
- Web is NOT a separate package. One Expo codebase serves web + Android + iOS; web is 'expo export -p web' / 'expo start --web' via Metro + react-native-web. Web-first is a build/deploy choice, not a filesystem split.
- RENAME the planned apps/mobile -> apps/client (platform-neutral; 'mobile' undersells the web-first target). Affects .1, .2, .3 and epic acceptance text.
- Metro does NOT follow workspace packages by default: apps/client needs metro.config.js watchFolders (workspace root) + nodeModulesPaths so it can resolve @whoplayd/contracts. Folded into bootstrapping (do in .2/.3).
- Proxy must have CORS for the browser client (native wouldn't need it). Record on apps/proxy skeleton/README in .3; actual config is plan-level.

TOOLING (locked):
- npm workspaces (NOT pnpm); ESLint + Prettier (NOT Biome, eslint-config-expo for client); layout apps/client, apps/proxy, apps/retry-worker, packages/contracts.
- Internal packages under @whoplayd/* scope. Fold into bootstrapping.
- Pin Node for proxy + retry-worker runtimes via root .nvmrc + engines. Fold into bootstrapping (do in .1).
- packages/contracts CONSUMPTION (raw TS vs tsc build) and test runner stay plan.md work.

COMMITS / PUSH / AUTHOR:
- One Conventional Commit per closed issue with a 'Beads: <id>' footer (one-issue-one-commit default).
- NO Co-Authored-By / Claude co-author trailer on any commit (overrides Claude global default for this repo).
- Push is USER-TRIGGERED ONLY, never automatic/session-end. The bd-init CLAUDE.md block ('work is NOT complete until git push succeeds') MUST be softened in wp-s1l.8.

APP MOVE (.2): git mv into apps/client to preserve history; regenerate root lockfile after workspaces configured.

WSL/METRO: repo stays on Linux fs (/home/reece/...), not /mnt, for watchman/Metro perf.

SEQUENCING: .1 workspaces -> .2 move app -> .3 skeletons -> .4 ESLint/Prettier -> .5 Husky -> .6 CI -> .7 STYLE.md -> .8 CLAUDE.md. .gitignore already complete, so commit-per-issue can start immediately.

This session: capture-only. Mechanical children deferred.
close_reason: Interview complete. Captured: apps/client (renamed from apps/mobile; one Expo codebase serves web-first + Android, web is a build target not a package); Metro watchFolders/@whoplayd scope/Node pin/proxy-CORS-note folded into bootstrapping; npm workspaces + ESLint/Prettier reconfirmed; commit-per-issue with Beads footer and NO co-author trailer; user-triggered push (bd-init push mandate to be softened in wp-s1l.8); git mv for the app relocation; WSL/Metro Linux-fs caveat. Mechanical children deferred per user.

title: Complete CLAUDE.md standing-rules block

design:
Complete standing-rules text for CLAUDE.md, preserved here so the setup context doc is disposable.

STATE OF CLAUDE.md right now:
- The `## Workflow` section has ONLY its first paragraph. The second paragraph below is NOT yet present — add it.
- `bd init` also injected a `## Beads Issue Tracker` + `## Session Completion` block. That injected block MANDATES
  `git pull --rebase && git push` at the end of every session and says "work is NOT complete until git push
  succeeds." That conflicts with (a) the decision to hold commits until .gitignore/sequencing is settled, and
  (b) the project's own Commits discipline. Reconcile when doing this issue — do not leave both stances live.

--- ADD this second paragraph under the existing `## Workflow` heading ---

At the start of every session, check Beads state (open epic, open/closed issues) before proposing next steps —
don't assume continuity from a previous conversation, since sessions carry no memory of it. When an epic's
issues all appear closed, say so explicitly and confirm before opening the next epic's issues, rather than
proceeding silently. If a genuinely open product or architecture question comes up mid-implementation (not a
tooling question), surface it rather than deciding it unilaterally — same posture as the constitution's own
governance rule for conflicts.

--- ADD these two sections (after Workflow) ---

## Commits

Conventional Commits format (feat/fix/docs/chore/refactor/test), referencing the Beads issue being closed (e.g.
a footer line "Beads: <issue-id>"). One commit generally maps to one closed issue — not a hard rule, but the
default unit — so there's a traceable line from spec → contract → Beads issue → commit.

## Definition of done (implementation issues)

An issue isn't done because code exists for it. It's done when: it satisfies what its linked spec/contract
section requires, lint/typecheck/tests pass (including contract tests where applicable), and the commit
references the issue. See STYLE.md for naming and file-organization conventions.
acceptance_criteria: CLAUDE.md contains Workflow + Commits + Definition of done standing rules, persisting across sessions.
close_reason: CLAUDE.md updated with Workflow para 2, Commits, and Definition-of-done sections; Session Completion block softened to user-triggered push
